fragment:
The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Satoshi-era wallet served in a $260 billion lawsuit moves 75 BTC it held since 2011. The roughly $5 million transfer also spent the tiny payment used to deliver a court notice to the address in May. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin miners pay Paraguay $350 million a year, but AI is pushing them out. Contracts that sell power to a 4% slice of the world’s bitcoin mining at $44 a megawatt-hour expire on Dec. 31, 2027. Paraguay’s state utility calls the date final, and it has just signed a 15-year deal to power a Founders Fund-backed AI campus. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin plunges to $68,000 as Anthropic IPO frenzy adds to market jitters. Analysts see no direct link between Nvidia and bitcoin's decline, pointing instead to investor capital headed into Anthropic as well as a broader risk-off move. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

U.S. Senate Banking Committee races toward hearing on new SEC nominations. The committee that needs to advance President Donald Trump's nominees responded quickly to set his SEC picks for review next week. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin heads for sixth weekly loss as Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO looms. Bitcoin is down 21% this year as investors weigh Anthropic’s anticipated listing, Nvidia’s leadership upheaval and rising Fed rate hike expectations. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Kraken parent Payward says expansion outside crypto trading helps cushion revenue decline. While earnings and the company’s newly introduced financial performance measure remained below year-earlier levels, there are signs of improvement from the second quarter. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $67,238 with a -2.94% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,909.31 with a -2.10% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum lie flat following negative ETF flows - DL News
items.description:
Share

 Investors started January by pumping over $1.5 billion into US crypto ETFs.
 But this week they redeemed over $1.3 billion from the products.
 Bitcoin and Ethereum have now lost their gains.

It was all going so well.

Investors started 2026 by throwing over $1.5 billion in fresh cash at Bitcoin and Ethereum US exchange-traded funds over the space of two days. [...] The price of the two largest digital coins by market cap rose following the investment. But now, both assets are both lying flat after investors this week pulled $1.3 billion out of the Bitcoin funds and $351 million from their Ethereum counterparts, according to data from Farside Investors.

Bitcoin was recently priced at nearly $90,623, up 1% over the past week. Ethereum was trading for $3,093, unmoved over a seven-day period. It traded as high as $3,293 mid-week. [...] Hello! This chart will be available in a few moments

Bitcoin is lying flat. Source: CoinGecko.

The ETF redemptions come after a good start to the year following weeks of negative flows.

Crypto markets ended 2025 in the red after struggling to recover from a massive October sell-off when over $19 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated — the largest such liquidation event in the history of digital assets.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.
 Ethereum is outpacing Bitcoin's inflow rate by $525M annually, but closing Bitcoin's $44B cumulative lead would still take over 80 years. [...] Both Bitcoin and Ethereum funds have declined from their highs earlier in 2026. Bitcoin fund assets peaked at $128 billion in mid-January 2026, while Ethereum funds hit $21 billion the same day. Since then, both funds have dropped by about 15%.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.title: Crypto market selloff triggers $1.3 billion in futures liquidations as bitcoin falls below $70,000
items.description:
A broader risk-off move in digital assets intensifies early Friday as bitcoin falls to its lowest level since Aug. 19 and ether drops below $2,000. The decline coincides with a stronger U.S. dollar, rising expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase and renewed geopolitical tension in the Middle East.

## Highlights

## Market slide deepens amid dollar strength [...] ## Liquidations mount as macro and geopolitical risks rise

Expectations for tighter U.S. monetary policy strengthen after a hotter-than-expected U.S. consumer price index reading for October released earlier this week. The odds of a half-percentage-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December have increased, adding to pressure across speculative markets.

## Liquidations mount as macro and geopolitical risks rise [...] The broader crypto market also weakens. Ether trades below $2,000 for the first time since August, XRP hovers near $1 and Solana's SOL falls below $80, while smaller tokens including GT, Stacks and XMR drop 7% or more.

The pressure comes as the Dollar Index, or DXY, trades above 103, its highest level since April 2025. The index has risen nearly 2% since early October as stronger odds of Fed rate hikes weigh on liquidity-sensitive risk assets.

items.title: Matrix on Point: The U.S. Dollar Hegemony in Transition - Social Science Matrix
items.description: And yet today, we find ourselves at a potential inflection point. New monetary instruments backed by technology, declining trust in the U.S. as a global power, and shifting geopolitical strategies amid escalating conflict are forcing us to ask whether the era of unquestioned U.S. dollar hegemony might be coming to an end. [...] The second consequence of low interest rates is that, well, everybody, even outside the U.S., if they can borrow in dollars, they will, because it’s cheap to do so. And that’s going to imply that dollar funding is an important part of balance sheets for leveraged investors, think hedge funds or other risk-taking parts of the economy globally. But that means then that U.S. monetary policy, which is really about changing dollar interest rates, propagates internationally in important ways. [...] Namely, in crises, as you can imagine, global investors really want to hold dollar assets. It’s a safe store of value. But as they do that, what will happen is the dollar will strengthen in foreign exchange markets ’cause they’re buying up more dollars, but also it’ll drive down U.S. interest rates, dollar interest rates broadly, because you’re buying up all these assets, so you’re willing to hold them even at a lower interest rate, at a lower rate of return.
